children: Tamil Nadu secures fresh commitments across advanced manufacturing, technology and GCCs, with major projects expected to create high value employment
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s UK visit has resulted in investment commitments worth around Rs 12,300 crore, with projects expected to generate more than 9,400 jobs across the state.

The largest commitment came from Samvardhana Motherson International, which has signed an MoU to invest around Rs 11,000 crore over the next five years. The company plans to establish integrated design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly and logistics facilities across Tamil Nadu, creating nearly 7,000 jobs.

Professional services firm EY has committed Rs 1,000 crore to establish a Global Capability Centre in the state, expected to create more than 2,000 high value corporate roles. UK based Wilson Power Solutions has also signed a Rs 300 crore MoU for a manufacturing unit in Tiruvallur, with around 400 jobs expected to be created.
Swedish technology company Sigma Technology Group is expanding its digital services and engineering operations in Tamil Nadu, further adding to the state’s technology and skilled workforce ecosystem.

The investment push comes as Tamil Nadu seeks to strengthen its position as a hub for advanced manufacturing, technology and global capability operations. The state government has also highlighted the potential for the new projects to deepen local supply chains and create opportunities across engineering, manufacturing, logistics and corporate services.
